zh: 我喜欢吃饺子，你呢？

q: 这些饺子应该是你包的___？

en: You must have made these dumplings, right?

q: 我喜欢吃饺子，你___？
zh: 我喜欢吃饺子，你呢？
py: wǒ xǐ huan chī jiǎo zi nǐ ne

s_py: nǐ xiǎng hē diǎn shén me ma
zh: 你想喝点什么吗？
py: nǐ xiǎng hē diǎn shén me ma
en: Would you like something to drink?
why: Here 什么 means "something", not a question word, so the sentence is a yes/no question and 吗 is correct.

task: Add 一定 and an assuring final particle.
zh: 他一定会来的。
py: tā yí dìng huì lái de
en: He will definitely come.
why: 一定会...的 is the assurance pattern; the sentence ends with 的.

q: 我现在不吃辣___，医生不让我吃。
zh: 我现在不吃辣了，医生不让我吃。
py: wǒ xiàn zài bù chī là le yī sheng bù ràng wǒ chī
en: I don't eat spicy food any more; the doctor won't let me.
why: 不...了 means "not any more". 呢 would say the situation is unchanged.

q: 我们不太熟，你们过年吃饺子___？
zh: 我们不太熟，你们过年吃饺子吗？
py: wǒ men bù tài shú nǐ men guò nián chī jiǎo zi ma
en: We don't know each other well. Do you eat dumplings at New Year?
why: The speaker has no guess about their habits, so this is a neutral yes/no question: 吗. 吧 would mean 'you eat dumplings, I take it?', which the context rules out.

q: 我不想吃饺子___，换个别的吧。
zh: 我不想吃饺子了，换个别的吧。
py: wǒ bù xiǎng chī jiǎo zi le huàn gè bié de ba
en: I don't feel like dumplings any more; let's have something else.
why: 不想...了 says the wish has changed. 呢 would say it is still the case.

q: 现在才六点___，饭馆还没开门。
zh: 现在才六点呢，饭馆还没开门。
py: xiàn zài cái liù diǎn ne fàn guǎn hái méi kāi mén
en: It's only six o'clock; the restaurant isn't open yet.
why: 才 says it is earlier than expected, and 呢 closes that "still early" statement. 了 would claim a new situation and clashes with 才.

q: 别哭，下次你一定会吃到___。
zh: 别哭，下次你一定会吃到的。
py: bié kū xià cì nǐ yí dìng huì chī dào de
en: Don't cry; you'll definitely get some next time.
why: 一定会 plus final 的 is a firm promise about the future. 了 reports a change, and 吧 would only be a guess.

q: 他正在包饺子___，你等一会儿再打电话吧。
zh: 他正在包饺子呢，你等一会儿再打电话吧。
py: tā zhèng zài bāo jiǎo zi ne nǐ děng yī huì r zài dǎ diàn huà ba
en: He's wrapping dumplings right now; wait a bit before you call.
why: 正在 + verb shows an action in progress and takes 呢 at the end. 了 would turn it into a completed event, which clashes with 正在.

q: 餐厅今天没有鱼，明天___？
zh: 餐厅今天没有鱼，明天呢？
py: cān tīng jīn tiān méi yǒu yú míng tiān ne
en: The restaurant has no fish today. What about tomorrow?
why: "What about X?" after a negative answer is noun + 呢. 吗 would need a whole statement such as 明天有鱼吗.

s: 放心，我一定会请你吃饭了。
s_py: fàng xīn wǒ yí dìng huì qǐng nǐ chī fàn le
zh: 放心，我一定会请你吃饭的。
py: fàng xīn wǒ yí dìng huì qǐng nǐ chī fàn de
en: Rest assured, I will definitely treat you to dinner.
why: A promise about the future is 会...的. 了 reports a change, which does not fit 一定会.

q: 你想喝酒就喝___，反正今天过节。
zh: 你想喝酒就喝呗，反正今天过节。
py: nǐ xiǎng hē jiǔ jiù hē bei fǎn zhèng jīn tiān guò jié
en: If you want a drink, just have one; it's a holiday anyway.
why: 想...就... plus 呗 means "just do it, no big deal". 吗 would turn the sentence into a question, which the shrugging tone rules out.

q: 你先喝点汤___，菜马上就来。
zh: 你先喝点汤吧，菜马上就来。
py: nǐ xiān hē diǎn tāng ba cài mǎ shàng jiù lái
en: Why don't you have some soup first; the dishes are coming right up.
why: A gentle invitation to do something is a soft command with 吧. 吗 would ask a factual question.

q: 这么贵的菜，味道应该不错___。
zh: 这么贵的菜，味道应该不错吧。
py: zhè me guì de cài wèi dào yīng gāi bù cuò ba
en: Food this expensive should taste pretty good, I suppose.
why: 应该 plus a guess about the taste takes 吧. 吗 would ask a question, and 呢 would state something is still the case.

q: 过节___，吃得多一点有什么关系，明天再减肥。
zh: 过节嘛，吃得多一点有什么关系，明天再减肥。
py: guò jié ma chī dé duō yì diǎn yǒu shén me guān xi míng tiān zài jiǎn féi
en: It's a holiday, after all; what's wrong with eating a bit more? Diet tomorrow.
why: 嘛 gives the obvious reason that excuses the speaker. 吗 would make the first clause a question.

q: 这家店的人太多了，我们换一家饭馆___，不然要等一个小时。
zh: 这家店的人太多了，我们换一家饭馆吧，不然要等一个小时。
py: zhè jiā diàn de rén tài duō le wǒ men huàn yī jiā fàn guǎn ba bù rán yào děng yí gè xiǎo shí
en: This place is too crowded; let's switch to another restaurant, or we'll wait an hour.
why: The speaker proposes a plan, so 吧. 了 would report that we already switched, and 吗 would ask a question.

q: 你想吃什么___？
zh: 你想吃什么？
py: nǐ xiǎng chī shén me
en: What do you want to eat?
why: 什么 already makes this a question asking for information, so nothing is added. 吗 is only for turning a statement into a yes/no question.

s_py: jīn tiān de cài zhēn hǎo chī ma
zh: 今天的菜真好吃啊！
py: jīn tiān de cài zhēn hǎo chī a
en: Today's food is so good!
why: 真好吃 is an exclamation, and 吗 would make it a question. 啊 adds warmth.

s: 你们几点去吃团圆饭吗？
s_py: nǐ men jǐ diǎn qù chī tuán yuán fàn ma
zh: 你们几点去吃团圆饭？
py: nǐ men jǐ diǎn qù chī tuán yuán fàn
en: What time are you going to the reunion dinner?
why: 几点 asks for information, so 吗 cannot follow it.

q: 为什么大家过中秋节都要吃月饼___？
zh: 为什么大家过中秋节都要吃月饼呢？
py: wèi shén me dà jia guò zhōng qiū jié dōu yào chī yuè bǐng ne
en: Why does everybody eat mooncakes at Mid-Autumn, I wonder?
why: 为什么 makes the sentence a question, so 吗 cannot be used. 呢 makes a why-question sound curious and less blunt.

q: 孩子们都长大___，不再跟着大人去逛庙会了。
zh: 孩子们都长大了，不再跟着大人去逛庙会了。
py: hái zi men dōu zhǎng dà le bù zài gēn zhe dà rén qù guàng miào huì le
en: The children have all grown up and no longer follow the grown-ups to the temple fair.
why: 长大了 is a change: they are grown now. 呢 would suggest they are still growing up, which clashes with 不再.

q: 不想做饭就出去吃___。
zh: 不想做饭就出去吃呗。
py: bù xiǎng zuò fàn jiù chū qù chī bei
en: If you don't feel like cooking, just eat out, then.
why: ...就...呗 treats the answer as simple, with a shrug. 吗 would ask a question and 呢 would say the situation is still going on.

s_py: wǒ bù xiǎng chī le nǐ chī ba
zh: 我不想吃了，你吃吧。
py: wǒ bù xiǎng chī le nǐ chī ba
en: I don't want to eat any more; you go ahead.
why: 不想吃了 means a changed wish, and 吧 softly offers the food. Both particles are correct.

q: 今年春节你不回来，爸妈一定会想你___，记得多打电话。
zh: 今年春节你不回来，爸妈一定会想你的，记得多打电话。
py: jīn nián chūn jié nǐ bù huí lái bà mā yí dìng huì xiǎng nǐ de jì de duō dǎ diàn huà
en: If you don't come home this Spring Festival, Mum and Dad are bound to miss you; remember to call often.
why: 一定会 plus 的 is a confident prediction. 了 would announce that they now miss you, and 吧 would soften it into a guess.

q: 她才五岁___，你别让她吃那么辣的菜。
zh: 她才五岁嘛，你别让她吃那么辣的菜。
py: tā cái wǔ suì ma nǐ bié ràng tā chī nà me là de cài
en: She's only five, after all; don't let her eat food that spicy.
why: The speaker is stating the obvious reason, which is 嘛. 吗 would ask whether she is five.

q: 别关门，里面还有客人在吃饭___。
zh: 别关门，里面还有客人在吃饭呢。
py: bié guān mén lǐ miàn hái yǒu kè rén zài chī fàn ne
en: Don't close up; there are still guests eating inside.
why: 在 + verb marks an action in progress, and 呢 confirms it is still the case. 了 would announce a change, and 吗 would turn it into a question.

q: 烟花还没放___，大家再等一会儿，十二点才开始。
zh: 烟花还没放呢，大家再等一会儿，十二点才开始。
py: yān huā hái méi fàng ne dà jia zài děng yī huì r shí èr diǎn cái kāi shǐ
en: The fireworks haven't started yet; wait a little longer, they only begin at twelve.
why: 还没 + 呢 says "not yet, still waiting". 了 cannot go after 还没, and 吗 would ask a question instead of reassuring.

q: 如果我们十二个人都想在除夕吃火锅，这家店能订到位子___？
zh: 如果我们十二个人都想在除夕吃火锅，这家店能订到位子吗？
py: rú guǒ wǒ men shí èr gè rén dōu xiǎng zài chú xī chī huǒ guō zhè jiā diàn néng dìng dào wèi zi ma
en: If all twelve of us want hot pot on New Year's Eve, can this place book us a table?
why: No question word, no A-not-A and no 还是: a neutral yes/no question ends in 吗. 呢 cannot turn a statement into a yes/no question.

zh: 他一定会喜欢这道菜的。
py: tā yí dìng huì xǐ huan zhè dào cài de
en: He will definitely like this dish.
why: 一定会...的 gives the assurance, with 的 at the end. 了 would report a change.

q: 你一定饿了___？
zh: 你一定饿了吧？
py: nǐ yí dìng è le ba
en: You must be hungry, right?
why: 一定 expresses certainty, so the sentence is a guess seeking agreement: 吧. 吗 does not combine with 一定.

q: 相信我，这家饭馆的菜不会让你失望___。
zh: 相信我，这家饭馆的菜不会让你失望的。
py: xiāng xin wǒ zhè jiā fàn guǎn de cài bú huì ràng nǐ shī wàng de
en: Trust me, the food at this restaurant won't let you down.
why: 不会...的 reassures the listener. 了 would claim they are already disappointed, and 吧 would make the promise tentative.

q: 年夜饭以后，你们喝茶还是喝酒___？
zh: 年夜饭以后，你们喝茶还是喝酒？
py: nián yè fàn yǐ hòu nǐ men hē chá hái shi hē jiǔ
en: After the New Year's Eve dinner, will you drink tea or alcohol?
why: 还是 asks the listener to choose between two options, which makes the sentence a question already. 吗 cannot be added.

q: 她现在是一家饭馆的老板___，生意不错。
zh: 她现在是一家饭馆的老板了，生意不错。
py: tā xiàn zài shì yī jiā fàn guǎn de lǎo ban le shēng yi bù cuò
en: She's the owner of a restaurant now, and business is good.
why: 现在 + 是 + 了 marks the new status. 的 would not mark a change, and 吧 would be a guess.

s_py: kuài lái a jiǎo zi dōu yào liáng le
zh: 快来啊，饺子都要凉了！
py: kuài lái a jiǎo zi dōu yào liáng le
en: Come on, hurry, the dumplings are about to get cold!
why: 啊 is friendly urging here. 啊 can follow a command, which learners may doubt.

src_py: wǒ men qù fàn guǎn chī fàn
zh: 我们去饭馆吃饭吧。
py: wǒ men qù fàn guǎn chī fàn ba
en: Let's go to a restaurant to eat.
why: 吧 at the end turns a statement into a suggestion.

s_py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù ài chī jiǎo zi
zh: 我已经不爱吃饺子了。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù ài chī jiǎo zi le
en: I don't like dumplings any more.
why: 已经 with 不 describes a change, so 了 is needed at the end.

q: 没想到你还会做这么复杂的菜，你真厉害___！
zh: 没想到你还会做这么复杂的菜，你真厉害啊！
py: méi xiǎng dào nǐ hái huì zuò zhè me fù zá de cài nǐ zhēn lì hai a
en: I had no idea you could cook such a complicated dish. You're amazing!
why: An admiring exclamation with 真 takes 啊. 吗 would turn the praise into a question.

zh: 今天是中秋节嘛。
py: jīn tiān shì zhōng qiū jié ma
en: It's Mid-Autumn Festival today, after all.
why: 嘛 closes a statement of the obvious. 吗 would turn it into a question.

q: 你们今年大概也在家过年___？
zh: 你们今年大概也在家过年吧？
py: nǐ men jīn nián dà gài yě zài jiā guò nián ba
en: You're probably staying home for New Year this year too, I suppose?
why: 大概 means "probably", which signals a guess seeking agreement: 吧. 吗 would be a neutral question with no guess.

s_py: xíng ba nà jiù zài jiā chī huǒ guō
zh: 行吧，那就在家吃火锅。
py: xíng ba nà jiù zài jiā chī huǒ guō
en: All right then, let's have hot pot at home.
why: 行吧 gives in to a proposal, so 吧 is correct. It looks like a question, but it is not.
